title: Operation Mincemeat, 1943
sources: IWM: The war on paper, Operation Mincemeat
National WWII Museum: Secret Agents, Secret Armies, Operation Mincemeat (2022)

lines.text: In nineteen forty-three, British spies came up with a plan so strange it sounds made up. They would fool Hitler... with a dead man.
His name was Glyndwr Michael, a homeless Welshman who had died after swallowing rat poison.
British intelligence gave him a new life. Major William Martin, Royal Marines.
They filled his pockets with a whole love story. A photo of his fiancée, her letters, a receipt for an engagement ring, theatre ticket stubs.
Chained to him, a briefcase with secret letters. The Allies, they said, would invade Greece. Sicily was just a cover.
The truth was the exact opposite.
On April thirtieth, a submarine slipped him into the sea off the coast of Spain.
A fisherman found him. Spain was neutral... but full of German spies.
The letters were secretly opened, photographed and passed to the Germans. Then sealed again, like nobody touched them.
And Hitler bought it. He sent a panzer division all the way from France to Greece.
In July, the Allies hit Sicily. Hitler was still waiting for Greece.
In London, the message came back. Mincemeat had been swallowed.
The man who never was lies in a grave in Spain. For decades, it only said William Martin.
Today it carries his real name too. Glyndwr Michael. A man who helped change the war, without ever knowing it.
